Changelog

voipred.dev 0.0.2.9000

Breaking changes

  • nb() is renamed nb_val().
  • p_useful() and p_best() are removed: P(useful) and P(best) come from evpi(), as evpi(res)$p_useful and evpi(res)$p_best.
  • nb_val() has one input argument, predicted_risk: a vector of risks, a column name or a fitted model, or, for several models, a list() of these. The model argument is removed (give the fitted model as predicted_risk), and so are data frames and matrices of risks; c() of several models is refused with a message pointing to list().
  • The result of nb_val() holds one or more models: models (the labels) replaces label, risk is a matrix with one column per model, and estimates and counts have a model column.
  • The censoring argument of nb_val() is removed: cIPCW is used when cipcw is given, Kaplan-Meier otherwise.
  • cIPCW truncates censoring probabilities at min_prob = 0.02 (weights at most 50) by default; min_prob = NULL turns truncation off (the previous default).
  • nb_beta(): the parts not given are Beta(0, 0) (no prior information) instead of Beta(1, 1); nb_beta() is nb_improper().

New features

  • Several models in one call of nb_val(), as a list that can mix fitted models, column names and vectors of risks. print(), summary(), plot() and the value-of-information functions compare all of them; the models are drawn jointly. c() combines results computed separately.
  • Labels follow one procedure: label, the names in the list, the column name, the name in the call, then "Model 1", "Model 2", …
  • predict_function can be one function for every fitted model, or a list named by model. nb_val() stops before predicting if voipred has no way to predict from a model and no function is given for it, naming the models.
  • cipcw = ~ covariates: voipred fits a Cox model of the censoring times on those covariates (refitted in every draw of the value-of-information functions). cipcw also takes a fitted censoring model, and cipcw_control() is optional, for the other settings.
  • P(useful) and P(best) are computed only by evpi(), from the same draws as EVPI, and kept in its result as e$p_useful and e$p_best, each with print(), summary(), plot() and as.data.frame(); plot(e, type = "p_useful") and plot(e, type = "p_best") draw them. The separate functions p_useful() and p_best() are removed (breaking change). summary(e) shows EVPI only.
  • nb_informative(): the informative prior of bayesDCA, whose priors on the sensitivity and specificity change with the threshold (binary outcomes), as nb_val(prior = nb_informative()), with bayesDCA’s defaults; its shapes match bayesDCA’s exactly. For a binary outcome, the result of nb_val() holds the prior shapes used at each threshold (prior_shapes).
  • The EVSI output states the information before the future study (the prior updated with the validation data, as for EVPI) and after it (with the future study added).
  • Any survival model can be the censoring model of cIPCW (e.g. a random survival forest, with refit_function for the value-of-information functions); ?cipcw_control has an example with a forest. The outcome of a model is also read from the call that fitted it (e.g. ranger), so the check that a censoring model was fitted to censoring works for forests too.
  • Fix: the automatic refit of a flexsurvreg censoring model in the value-of-information functions starts from the original estimates (it could fail with the extreme weights of some draws).
  • Credible intervals: nb_val(..., interval = 0.95) keeps 95% credible intervals of NB_model, NB_all and delta_NB at each threshold (default NULL: none), from n_sim draws: the posterior for a binary outcome, the Bayesian bootstrap for survival and competing-risks outcomes. print() and summary() show them, as.data.frame() has the bounds, and plot(bands = TRUE) draws them as shaded bands (the default plot has none). Every use of the intervals warns and recommends value-of-information analysis (evpi()).
  • per: print(), summary(), as.data.frame() and plot() of the results of nb_val(), evpi() and evsi() can express the net benefit, EVPI and EVSI per per patients (default 1, per patient; e.g. per = 100000). The headers and the y axes say the scale; as.data.frame() keeps the per-patient columns and adds the scaled ones (<column>_per_<per>); the results themselves stay per patient. The default can be set with options(voipred.per = ).
  • Plots take optional colours, by label or in order: colors =.
  • Clear messages when plotly (interactive plots) or patchwork (stacked panels) is not installed, with how to install them.
  • The joint posterior of several models stops with a message before it would need more than about 2 GB of memory.
